chapter: Chicago clubs, entertainers and tent shows
title: The Pekin Inn and mob control of Chicago clubs
summary: The Pekin Inn was a Chinese restaurant where musicians gathered after hours; he guesses gangsters ran most Chicago clubs.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Now did you ever go to the Pekin Inn?
Yes.
What was that like, was it a Chinese place?

It was a Chinese place, yes. It was a joint where the musicians would gather there quite a lot and they would have a few players, sometimes would play the Pekin Inn. But it was mostly a Chinese -- where you get good Chinese food.
Now that was common in those days, wasn't it --
Oh, yes.
-- to have black music in Chinese places?
Right, that's right. Yes. Very
common.
joints.
And what were they called, chopsuey
Well, yes. Well the Pekin Inn, they didn't call themselves a chopsuey place at all, it was just the Pekin Inn.
Uh-huh.
It was very popular, quite a lot of the musicians would go to meet at the Pekin Inn, after hours.
Uh-huh.
And some time they had 4 little playing sessions there.
Now were these places, like the Pekin, were they run by Chinese people?
I -- that I don't really know. You never knew who ran a lot of the clubs in Chicago, at that time.
Uh-huh.

But I have an idea that the mob, you know the people, the gangsters, or whatever you all them, had a lot to do with most all the clubs in Chicago. At that time, cause they were supplying, you know, beer and stuff to all of them, see, they probably ran them.
